operational-example.copy: Use Menu for compact action sets attached to a trigger, especially when actions are contextual, secondary, grouped, or permission dependent.

scenario.title: Driver row actions
scenario.meta: Contextual actions without leaving the table
rationale: Menu keeps secondary actions near their object without turning every row into a toolbar.
The ZIP reference defines the compact floating surface, item height, separators, hover state, and scale motion.
Actions must be real buttons with menu semantics, not a visual list with fake affordances.

items.rule: Opens the contextual action list and exposes expanded state.
Floats near the trigger with radius, border, shadow, motion, and compact padding.
Uses clear labels, optional icons, disabled state, and keyboard focus.
Groups actions only when the group changes meaning or risk.
Marks destructive action with semantic tone and hover surface.

items: Use a trigger with aria-haspopup menu and aria-expanded.
Use role menu and menuitem for the floating panel and actions.
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
Disabled items remain visible only when they explain unavailable actions.
Do not place long forms, filters, or rich content inside Menu.

variants.copy: Menu variants describe the action model: actions, grouped actions, selection commands, danger grouping, and icon-only trigger usage.

states.copy: Menu states cover trigger availability, panel lifecycle, keyboard focus, disabled actions, and closed state.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant sets action grouping; state defines whether the panel is available, open, focused, disabled, or closed.

full-width.copy: Menu belongs to its trigger, not the full page. The available region may be full-width, but the panel stays compact.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Menu stays compact across viewports. On phones, prefer fewer items and escalate long sets to Drawer or Bottom Sheet.

viewport-organization.copy: Keep Menu near the object it controls. If the action set needs explanation, inputs, or review, use Drawer or Dialog.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use short menus only; escalate complex sets.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep panels within safe margins and away from nav.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use row or toolbar triggers for dense operations.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify trigger label, variant, state, alignment, danger grouping, disabled items, and close behavior.

api-foundations.copy: Menu API exposes trigger, items, variant, state, alignment, disabled state, avatar trigger metadata, danger tone, and separators while Design System foundations own surface, motion, keyboard, icon, and tone rules.

props.name: variant
props.type: actions | grouped | selection | danger | icon-trigger | avatar-trigger
props.notes: Action model shown by the menu.

props.name: avatarName
props.notes: Name rendered by Avatar when variant is avatar-trigger.

props.name: avatarStatus
props.notes: Avatar status rendered by the trigger when variant is avatar-trigger.

props.name: avatarSize
props.notes: Avatar size rendered by the trigger when variant is avatar-trigger.

props.name: density
props.notes: Controls trigger, panel, and item scale for sm, md, and lg contexts.

props.name: align
props.notes: Panel alignment relative to the trigger.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.notes: Called when local open state changes.

props.name: onSelect
props.notes: Called when an item is selected.

groups.title: Use
items: Group destructive actions with clear separation.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not put forms or long explanations in Menu.
Do not hide primary actions only inside Menu.
Do not use disabled items unless they explain permissions.

groups.title: Review
items: Check keyboard opening, Escape close, item focus, disabled state, and danger contrast.
Confirm long menus escalate to Drawer or Bottom Sheet.
Verify panel stays anchored without clipping.

rejectIf: Menu contains a form or rich content.
Primary process action is hidden only in Menu.
Trigger or items use fake buttons.
Raw color, spacing, shadow, or motion values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Menu as compact contextual action access: agents can use it for secondary commands while humans confirm item priority, destructive grouping, and whether a Drawer is more appropriate.
canDecide: Use Menu for compact secondary action sets.
Use separators when action risk or category changes.
Escalate long or explanatory content to Drawer.
mustAsk: A menu item changes money, access, or legal state.
The set needs more than a compact action list.
The trigger is the only way to reach a primary action.
rejectIf: Menu contains forms, paragraphs, or complex filters.
Danger actions are visually mixed with safe actions.
Open, close, keyboard, or disabled behavior is undefined.
miel.handoff: I am using Menu for contextual secondary actions. Please confirm item order, destructive grouping, disabled behavior, alignment, and escalation rules.
